claims.text: FAA's current AI/ML technical-discipline page says its work includes collaboration with industry, other government agencies, standards-development organizations and academia to advance understanding of AI algorithms, data and model performance in the aviation certification context.
claims.scope: FAA public technical-discipline page, captured 2026-09-22; statement of activity, not a completed standard or approval outcome
claims.challenge: Check later FAA roadmap versions, consensus-standard publications and certification decisions. This page cannot establish whether enough qualified people exist, what any committee has concluded, or whether an adequate method has been accepted for a particular high-criticality function.

claims.text: On the captured EASA CRT status page, RMT.0742's DS.AI NPA 2025-07(B) is still labelled proposed and 'awaiting responses to comments'; the page therefore does not show a final published DS.AI AMC/GM result.
claims.scope: EASA CRT page captured 2026-09-22; online rulemaking-status observation for RMT.0742, not a conclusion about all EASA AI approvals
claims.challenge: Recheck EASA's rulemaking portal and Official Publication pages immediately before publication. A final decision, CRD, AMC/GM or other page may supersede this time-sensitive status display.

claims.text: U.S. law requires a motor-vehicle or equipment manufacturer/distributor to certify compliance with applicable federal motor-vehicle safety standards at delivery, and prohibits a certificate the issuer knows, with reasonable care, is materially false or misleading.
claims.scope: 49 U.S.C. § 30115(a), current preliminary U.S. Code page captured 2026-09-22; certification of applicable FMVSS compliance
claims.challenge: Pair with the specific FMVSS, defect/recall provisions, exemptions and state operation authorities relevant to any example. This statute cannot be paraphrased as manufacturer certification that a trained model is safe in every scenario.

claims.text: In a 2025 interpretation, NHTSA states that it does not pre-approve new motor vehicles, equipment or ADS technologies, while describing manufacturer self-certification to applicable FMVSS and NHTSA's safety-defect authority.
claims.scope: NHTSA nonbinding interpretation of a particular ADAS/FMVSS No. 108 question; used only to describe the stated federal oversight boundary
claims.challenge: Obtain a full source snapshot and compare current NHTSA rules, exemptions and investigations. Do not use this specific interpretation as an approval of driverless deployment or as a substitute for any required applicable-standard evidence.

claims.text: SAE's public page for J3321_202603 shows that a new ground-vehicle AI/ML V&V document exists, but describes it as an information report with no mandatory requirements and general V&V methods.
claims.scope: SAE public product-page scope, 2026-03-16; no licensed-text or regulator-recognition claim
claims.challenge: Acquire the authorized text and check SAE's document classification and any later revision. Its existence counters a blanket claim that no automotive AI/ML V&V guidance exists, but its public scope cannot establish a complete accepted certification method.
